content:
Both try? and hint seem to try a list of a bunch of random tactics. As far as I can tell, try? is defined in core while hint is defined in mathlib, and hint seems to be more powerful. Is this correct?

There's also trivial (not to be confused with the term docs#trivial, which is shorthand for True.intro) which tries some tactics, but these generally tend to be less powerful.
hint is meant to be replaced by try?, I thought it was already explicitly deprecated.

I was recalling messages like #PR reviews > #22365 hint tactics @ 💬 saying so -- though #PR reviews > feat: register mathlib tactics with try? @ 💬 contradicts it, so I guess the intentions maybe changed somewhere along the way and maybe try? is indeed not meant to obsolete it anymore, but I don't know then what the difference between them is intended to be.

My intention is that hint is deprecated and will be removed, but this doesn't seem to have happened yet. Joachim is working on making try? even better, and there is already an extensibility mechanism to add library-defined tactics into try?.

Would any be game to take on deprecating hint?

Or to identify specific cases where hint is working better than try?, so we can remedy these?
Well I just tried hint recently, and it gave me a list of options that I could use, whereas try? just gave me the first option that succeeded

Low hanging fruit: hint has better discoverability

#help tactic "hint"
/-
syntax "hint"... [Mathlib.Tactic.Hint.hintStx]
  The `hint` tactic tries every tactic registered using `register_hint <prio> tac`,
  and reports any that succeed.
-/
#help tactic "try?"
/-
syntax "try?"... [Lean.Parser.Tactic.tryTrace]
-/
